guide.summary: Notion uses a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow through a public connection you create in the Developer portal. No review is needed to start authorizing users. A security review applies only if you want a Marketplace listing, which is optional. The main traps are an installation scope setting that cannot be changed after creation, refresh token rotation, and per-user authorization where users only see pages they have full access to.

reasons_to_bring_own: You want your own Marketplace listing. That requires Any workspace installation scope and a Notion security review.
You want to limit installs to a specific set of workspaces, which is fixed when the connection is created.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Use Composio managed auth; you do not need your own app yet because Notion requires no review to start OAuth, so your own connection only matters once you want your own Marketplace listing or workspace restrictions.

prerequisites.text: A Notion account and a development workspace to name in the registration form.
At least one redirect URI ready to enter in the OAuth configuration section. Public connection OAuth will not work without one.
A decision on installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) before you create the connection.
Workspace owner role is required only if you create an internal connection instead of a public one.

redirect_uri_rules: Redirect URIs are configured in the Developer portal's OAuth configuration section when you create the connection.
Send redirect_uri in the token request if it was in the authorization URL or if multiple redirect URIs are configured. Otherwise it is not allowed.
If the user cancels, Notion redirects to your redirect URI with error=access_denied.

blockers.text: Installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) cannot be changed after the connection is created. Only Any workspace makes you eligible for Marketplace listing.
blockers.workaround: Decide before creating the connection. If unsure, choose Any workspace, since listing stays optional. If you choose wrong, create a new connection.

blockers.text: A 429 with public_api_request_blocked means Notion restricted the connection's API access. Retrying will not help.
blockers.workaround: Stop retrying and contact Notion support.

blockers.text: Each user in a workspace must authorize the connection individually. One admin install does not cover the team.
blockers.workaround: Design onboarding so every user runs the OAuth flow themselves.

app_specific_gotchas.text: Installation scope is locked at creation and decides whether you can ever list on the Marketplace.
Refresh rotates tokens. Every refresh returns a new refresh token, so you must store it or lose access.
The authorization URL must always include owner=user, and token requests use HTTP Basic Auth with client ID and secret, not body parameters.
The page picker only shows pages the user has full access to, so your agent may see less than the user expects.
There is no OIDC or OAuth discovery document on notion.so. Hardcode the endpoints.

limits: Full OAuth works without Marketplace submission or review. An unlisted public connection is usable as-is.
Each user in a workspace must authorize individually. One install does not cover the whole workspace.
Users can only share pages they have full access to in the page picker.
With Selected workspaces scope, only the workspaces chosen at creation can install, and this cannot be changed.
If Notion restricts API access (429 public_api_request_blocked), retries will not help and you must contact support.
unapproved_mode.breaks_at: Nothing breaks for unlisted use. The wall is a Marketplace listing, which requires a Notion security review of undocumented length. If you chose Selected workspaces at creation, that route is closed and you would need a new connection.

steps.title: Prepare the registration inputs
steps.detail_md: Draft what the portal form will ask for: a connection name, the development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities (c28). List every callback URL you will use (local dev, staging, production), because redirect URIs are configured in the OAuth configuration section and public OAuth needs at least one (c12, c19). Keep the list short: with **more than one** redirect URI configured, every token request must include `redirect_uri` (c6).

steps.title: Decide installation scope (irreversible)
steps.detail_md: Choose **Any workspace** or **Selected workspaces only**. This cannot be changed after creation (c9, c29). Selected workspaces locks the connection to a set you choose now (c13). Any workspace lets any workspace install it and is the only path to an optional Marketplace listing (c13, c31). For an agent that arbitrary users will connect, Any workspace is the practical choice. The agent can lay out this trade-off, but only you should make the call.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail_md:
Log in to the Notion Developer portal (the connections page responded at `https://app.notion.com/developers/connections`, c39). Go to **Build > Connections** and click **Create new connection** (c26, c27). Fill in:

- name
- development workspace
- redirect URI(s) in the OAuth configuration section
- installation scope
- capabilities

(c28, c35)

Workspace owner rights are documented as required only for *internal* connections (c17, c33). The claims do not say what role a public connection needs.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret; optionally set a template URL
steps.detail_md: After creation, open the **Configuration** tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret (c30). Store the secret in your secrets manager, not in code. If you want a duplicate-on-install template, set the optional template URL in **Basic information** under the distribution settings on the same tab (c36).

steps.title: Implement the authorization redirect
steps.detail_md:
Build the authorize URL on `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize` (c1). Use the authorization code flow with `response_type=code` and always set `owner=user` (c3, c4). A probe with a fake client_id was redirected to Notion's install-integration page, which confirms the endpoint is live (c42).

Notion serves no OIDC or OAuth discovery document on notion.so, so hardcode the endpoints (c40, c41).

Handle cancellation: Notion redirects back with `error=access_denied` (c11).

steps.title: Implement code exchange and refresh with rotation
steps.detail_md:
Exchange the code at `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token`, authenticating with HTTP Basic using the client ID and secret (c2, c5, c38). The response contains both an access_token and a refresh_token (c20).

Include `redirect_uri` only if it was in the authorize URL or if you configured multiple redirect URIs. Otherwise it is not allowed (c6).

Refresh against the same endpoint. Each refresh returns a **new** refresh token, so persist it atomically and discard the old one (c2, c7).

steps.title: Handle per-user auth and hard blocks
steps.detail_md:
Model tokens per user, not per workspace. Each user must authorize individually (c10, c37). The page picker only shows pages the user has full access to, so surface a clear message when expected pages are missing (c37).

Treat a 429 with `public_api_request_blocked` as fatal: do not retry. Alert someone to contact Notion support (c23).

steps.title: Test end to end with real accounts
steps.detail_md: Log in with a real Notion account, run the full flow, pick pages and confirm API calls work. Also run the token refresh path and a cancel (access_denied). No Marketplace submission or review is needed to start OAuth authorization (c8). The connection is usable and shareable with users in its installation scope at this point (c13, c32).

steps.title: Optional: submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail_md: Skip this unless you want discoverability. Listing is separate from OAuth distribution and is managed in the **Listings** section (c16). It requires an Any workspace connection and a Notion security review (c31, c32). The agent can draft listing copy, but submitting it is your job.

steps.title: Optional: wait for Notion security review
steps.detail_md: Notion runs a security review before a Marketplace listing goes live (c32). How long it takes is **not documented** in the available claims. The 0 in the estimate means unknown, not instant. Your OAuth integration keeps working during the review (c32).

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: Yes, Notion requires a public integration to go through its review process before any user outside the workspace that created it can connect.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say marketplace submission or review is not required to start OAuth, and a public connection can be created and used without listing; a security review applies only before Marketplace listing.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Notion review typically takes about 5 business days, though I'd expect it to run up to 2 weeks in busy periods.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention review turnaround times.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: While unapproved, a public integration can only be installed in the workspace that owns it, with no more than 1 external workspace allowed for testing.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say public connections can be installed in any workspace within their installation scope (any workspace or selected workspaces) and can be used without listing, which contradicts the owner-only restriction; no 1-external-workspace limit is mentioned.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Creating and submitting a Notion integration is free, with no paid plan or fee required.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not address fees for creating an integration; the only cost claim concerns SCIM provisioning being Enterprise-only.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: Submission requires a privacy policy URL, a company website, and a demo video, but no formal business verification step.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention privacy policy, company website, demo video, or business verification; the registration form is described as requiring only name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope, and capabilities.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS and exactly match one of the URIs registered in the integration settings, with no wildcards allowed.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say redirect URIs are configured in the Developer portal's OAuth configuration and that redirect_uri is conditionally required in the token request, but they do not state HTTPS, exact-match, or wildcard rules.
